title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms
summary: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision published finalised Basel III reforms in December 2017 to address pre-crisis regulatory framework shortcomings. A key objective is reducing excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs) that undermined stakeholder confidence during the global financial crisis. The reforms enhance standardised approaches for credit and operational risk, constrain internally-modelled approaches, and add a finalised leverage ratio and robust capital floor.
key_points: Published December 2017; implementation phased from 1 January 2022 through 1 January 2027 for output floor (50% to 72.5%)
Revisions to standardised approach for credit risk and CVA framework effective 1 January 2022
Revisions to IRB framework and leverage ratio (revised exposure definition) effective 1 January 2022 and 2025 respectively
G-SIB buffer effective 1 January 2022; 1.06 scaling factor for IRB RWA amounts will no longer apply upon implementation

Three overarching principles: strengthen bank regulation/supervision globally, actively seek stakeholder views, conduct comprehensive impact assessment without significantly increasing overall capital requirements
why_it_matters: This is the definitive regulatory standard for global banking capital adequacy post-financial crisis. Banks' capital planning, risk management frameworks, and competitive dynamics are directly affected. The output floor and leverage ratio requirements shape how banks allocate assets and manage balance sheets, with downstream effects on credit availability and market liquidity.
macro_context: By maintaining overall capital requirements at current levels while improving framework robustness, the Committee aimed to avoid constraining bank lending to the real economy while still enhancing financial stability.
market_structure_context: The reforms directly affect market structure by constraining RWA variability (improving comparability of bank capital ratios), finalising the leverage ratio framework, and introducing the output floor which limits benefits from internal models. These changes impact how banks optimise capital across asset classes.
important_numbers: 1 January 2022: Credit risk standardised approach, CVA framework, G-SIB buffer
1 January 2025: Revised leverage ratio exposure definition
